title: Philippine president declares energy emergency as impact of Iran war felt
byline: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr has declared a national energy emergency in response to the US-Israel war on Iran ⁠and what he called the “imminent danger” posed to the country’s energy supply.

title: Sri Lanka reiterates no diplomatic level invitation made to Iranian vessel
byline: The government yesterday reiterated that Sri Lanka did not make a diplomatic level invitation for Iranian vessel ‘IRIS Dena’ to visit Sri Lanka other than a cordial and oral invitation made by Navy Commander at an event in India.

title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes have killed 1,072 since March 2
byline: Lebanon’s Health Ministry said Tuesday that the death toll from ongoing Israeli strikes on the country has risen to 1,072, with 2,966 people wounded since March 2, Anadolu reports.

title: Meta loses major child safety trial, ordered to pay $375 million
byline: A New Mexico jury found Meta liable Tuesday for misleading consumers about the safety of its platforms and endangering children.

title: Russia’s Deputy Energy Minister here tomorrow amidst talks on fuel purchase from Russia
byline: Amidst ongoing talks on the procurement of fuel from Russia, Russia’s Deputy Energy Minister Roman Marshavin is scheduled to visit Sri Lanka tomorrow (26), Daily Mirror learns.

title: Trump says Vance and Rubio lead Iran talks and expects deal soon
byline: U.S. President Donald Trump said that Vice President J.D. Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are leading talks with Iran aimed at ending the war, expressing optimism about reaching a deal in the coming days.

title: Met. Dept. warns of high temperatures next month
byline: The Meteorology Department has warned that high temperatures affecting the human body are expected to continue throughout next month, Department Director Meryl Mendis said.

title: Sri Lanka, Russia to strike oil purchasing deal next week
byline: Against the backdrop of disruptions to global oil supply, Sri Lanka expects to finalize an oil purchase deal with Russia next week, an official said.

title: Defending champion RCB sold for record-breaking Rs. 16,700 crore IPL deal
byline: Indian Premier League (IPL) franchise Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) has been bought by a consortium comprising the Aditya Birla Group (ABG), The Times of India Group (ToI), Bolt Ventures (Bolt) and Blackstone’s Perpetual Private Equity Strategy (BXPE, Blackstone) for a valuation of $1.78 billion, which translates to approximately Rs. 16,706 crore.

title: Hatton pharmacy owner arrested with 1,400 intoxicating pills
byline: A pharmacy owner in Hatton was arrested on suspicion of selling intoxicating pills to youths without a valid medical prescription during a raid carried out by officers of the Hatton Divisional Anti-Corruption Unit yesterday (March 24).

title: Oil at $150 will trigger global recession, says boss of financial giant BlackRock
byline: If the price of oil hits $150 a barrel it will trigger a global recession, the boss of US financial giant BlackRock has told the BBC.

title: Rs. 15 mn cigarette haul seized at BIA; two passengers arrested
byline: Two Sri Lankan passengers who attempted to smuggle foreign-made cigarettes worth nearly Rs. 15 million through the Green Channel at the arrival terminal of the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) were arrested by Airport Customs officers today (25).

title: Russia launches 948 drones at Ukraine in largest attack over 24-hour period
byline: Russia has launched the largest aerial attack on Ukraine over a 24-hour period since the war began, hitting cities across the country with 948 drones.

title: Mattala Airport field visit set for next week as Gulf carriers weigh alternative transit hubs
byline: With a crucial field visit scheduled for next week, the Sri Lankan government is advancing discussions with major Gulf carriers to utilise Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport (MRIA) as an alternative transit hub amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, Mirror Business learns.

title: Teachers’ absence at PM meeting: Tangalle education zone seeks explanation
byline: The Zonal Education Office in Tangalle has instructed all school principals in the Tangalle Education Zone to submit reports explaining the non-participation of teachers at a special meeting held on March 15, 2026, at the Tangalle Town Hall under the patronage of Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya.

title: 'Illustrious' Salah to leave Liverpool at the end of the season
byline: Mohamed Salah will leave Premier League champions Liverpool at the end of the season, the Egypt forward announced on Tuesday as he started a farewell to what the club called nine ’’illustrious’’ years at Anfield.

title: India-US consortium buys IPL Royal Challengers Bengaluru for $1.7bn
byline: A consortium of investors, including US asset management giant Blackstone, on Tuesday announced the takeover of Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB), one of the founding clubs of Indian Premier League, for nearly $1.8 billion.

title: Modi, President Dissanayake discuss West Asia crisis, energy security
byline: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a telephone conversation with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, during which they discussed the evolving situation in West Asia, with a particular focus on disruptions impacting global energy security.

title: Blow to Italian PM Giorgia Meloni as she suffers referendum defeat
byline: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has conceded defeat in a government-promoted referendum to reform the justice system.

title: Iran arrests 466 over online activities amid war with US and Israel
byline: Iranian authorities announced on Tuesday the arrest of 466 people accused of seeking to destabilise the country through their online activity, state media reported, as the war with the US and Israel ground on.

title: President pushes fast-track law to destroy seized narcotics
byline: A meeting between Anura Kumara Dissanayake and a special committee tasked with removing legal barriers to the rapid destruction of seized narcotics was held at the Presidential Secretariat.

title: Use electricity sparingly as record demand hits 3,089 MW
byline: The public has been urged to use electricity sparingly as Sri Lanka grapples with record-high power demand driven by prevailing dry weather conditions.

title: Philippines declares energy emergency over Iran conflict
byline: The Philippines has declared a state of national energy emergency, citing the ’’imminent danger’’ posed to the country’s fuel supplies by the conflict in the Middle East.

title: ADB raises Sri Lanka allocation to USD 480m, releases USD 200m
byline: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has agreed to increase the allocation approved for Sri Lanka for this year from USD 380 million to USD 480 million and to promptly release USD 200 million in view of the prevailing situation, the President’s Media Division (PMD) said.

title: Fuel price hike based on pricing formula – CPC
byline: The recent fuel price increase was implemented in line with the pricing formula, said Managing Director of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation, Mayura Neththikumara.

title: Ex-SriLankan chairman arrested for using airline funds to pay Minister’s fuel bills
byline: A former Chairman of SriLankan Airlines was arrested this morning (24) by officers of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) over alleged corruption.

title: Rajasthan Royals sold in a massive US$1.6 billion deal ahead of IPL 2026
byline: Rajasthan Royals has been acquired by Kal Somani for a whopping price of US$1.6 billion, making it one of the most valued franchises in the Indian Premier League. The deal has been closed with only a few days left before the commencement of the 2026 edition of the marquee T20 tournament. Notably, Somani was a minority shareholder in the franchise earlier but has now gained full ownership.

title: Contract awarded to upgrade Colombo Fort Railway Station
byline: The Cabinet has granted approval to award the contract for upgrading passenger facilities at the Colombo Fort Railway Station to MAGA Engineering (Pvt) Ltd, the government said.

title: Kim vows to ‘irreversibly’ cement North Korea’s nuclear status
byline: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has pledged to irreversibly cement his country’s status as a nuclear power while maintaining a hard-line stance toward South Korea, which he called the “most hostile” state, state media said Tuesday.

title: Court of Appeal dismisses SriLankan Airlines’ writ petition over salary cuts
byline: A writ application filed by SriLankan Airlines Limited, challenging the determination of the Assistant Commissioner of Labour relating to salary reductions implemented in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, including those affecting pilots, has been dismissed by the Court of Appeal.

title: Iran war: US reportedly offers 15-point plan to end war
byline: The Iranian military has dismissed reports of US-Iran peace negotiations, casting doubts over the 15-point peace plan reportedly put forward by the White House.

title: Sri Lanka says it has no vessels to import fuel from Iran
byline: While appreciating Iran’s offer to provide Sri Lanka with oil and other necessary goods, Cabinet Spokesman Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said yesterday that country’s that own vessels can benefit from such opportunities and that Sri Lanka is not having such an ability.

title: Heavy influx of tourists at Ravana Ella
byline: A heavy influx of foreign tourists was experienced yesterday at Ravana Ella.

title: Infant’s body discovered in Meegaswewa
byline: The Meegaswewa Police have initiated an investigation following the discovery of an infant’s body in a private land in Palliyagodella, Meegaswewa.

title: US expected to send thousands more soldiers to Middle East, sources say
byline: The Pentagon is expected to send ​thousands of soldiers from the U.S. Army’s elite 82nd Airborne Division to the Middle East, two people familiar with the ‌matter told Reuters on Tuesday, adding to a massive U.S. military buildup even as President Donald Trump talks about a possible deal with Tehran to end the war.

title: First 4D angio CT suite in South Asia installed at Sri Jayewardenepura hospital
byline: The Sri Jayewardenepura General Hospital has installed the first 4D Angio CT suite in the South Asian region, marking a major milestone in advanced medical care in the country. The state-of-the-art system, funded by the Japanese government at a cost of Rs. 925 million, was inaugurated yesterday (24) by Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa, with the Japanese Ambassador to Sri Lanka, H.E. Akio Isomata, also in attendance.

title: Health services at cross roads as doctors convene emergency meeting
byline: Sri Lanka’s health services are at a critical juncture as doctors prepare to convene an emergency General Committee meeting today (25), with several key decisions expected amid a deepening crisis.

title: Lamborghinis stranded in Sri Lanka as war disrupts Asia’s used-car trade
byline: The U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran last month plunged the Middle East into crisis, disrupted global shipping routes and spawned a series of headaches for Umar Ali Hyder Ali’s used-car business in Japan.

title: Thousands of TB cases remain undetected in Sri Lanka: WHO
byline: In Sri Lanka, the World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that around 14,000 new TB cases occur annually, but only 8,500–9,500 cases are currently diagnosed, leaving about 5,000 patients undetected in the community. This significant gap underscores the need for intensified efforts to combat tuberculosis in the country.

title: Medicine prices may surge amid forex, fuel and Middle East crisis: Dr. Sanjeewa
byline: A sharp increase in medicine prices in the local market could be inevitable due to the ongoing Middle East crisis, foreign exchange shortages, fuel price hikes, and the rising cost of goods and services, the Federation of Medical and Civil Rights Doctors’ Trade Unions Chairman amd Specialist Dr. Chamal Sanjeewa, claimed.

title: Python dance sparks legal action; suspect released on bail
byline: The Colombo Additional Magistrate H.D.D.J. Premaratne yesterday ordered that the suspect, a young woman accused of engaging in a dance performance while holding a python around her neck in a cruel manner during a ’Avurudu Kumara Kumariya’ pageant held in the Colombo area, be released on bail.

title: Oil prices Tumble back below $100 on ceasefire optimism
byline: Oil prices fell sharply in early asian trade on Wednesday, with both major benchmarks dropping more than 5% as traders reacted to signs of potential de-escalation in the Middle East conflict as well as a crude inventory build in the U.S.

title: “No More Excuses”: court flags tech failure, directs authorities to take action
byline: Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama yesterday directed the Police Narcotics Bureau to immediately inform relevant authorities that Sri Lanka lacks the technical capability to analyze satellite phone data, following a report submitted by the Government Analyst’s Department.

title: Philippine president declares energy emergency as impact of Iran war felt
byline: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr has declared a national energy emergency in response to the US-Israel war on Iran ⁠and what he called the “imminent danger” posed to the country’s energy supply.

title: How is Sri Lanka responding to the Israel–Iran conflict: Day 26
byline: As tensions escalate between Israel and Iran, Sri Lanka has taken a series of diplomatic, aviation and precautionary measures to manage potential fallout and safeguard its citizens. Here is how Sri Lanka is responding.

title: All examinations to be conducted as scheduled: Cabinet Sub-Committee decides
byline: The Cabinet Sub-Committee Appointed to Streamline the Public Service has decided to ensure that examinations are conducted as scheduled.

title: Police stop outdoor class in Hatton on public holiday
byline: Hatton police intervened today to stop an outdoor class conducted by two teachers on a public holiday declared by the government.

title: Australia to restrict entry to some Iranian visa holders
byline: The federal government will temporarily restrict some Iranian visitor visa holders from entering the country for six months, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke has announced.

title: Railway union urges no train fare hike
byline: The Sri Lanka Railway Station Masters’ Union (SLRSMU) today requested the government not to revise train fares, stating that a large number of people have turned to railway transport for their daily travel due to the rising cost of living.

title: Suresh Sallay admitted to National hospital
byline: Major General (Retired) Suresh Sallay, the former Head of the State Intelligence Service (SIS), has been admitted to the Colombo National Hospital following a sudden illness, sources said.

title: Nine Vietnamese arrested in Poddala fraud bust
byline: Nine Vietnamese nationals were arrested in the Godakanda area of Poddala on Tuesday (24) for allegedly engaging in online financial fraud, police said.

title: Water levels in Castlereagh, Maussakelle reservoirs drop sharply amid dry weather
byline: The water levels of the Castlereagh and Maussakelle reservoirs are rapidly declining due to the dry weather conditions prevailing in the central hills, an official in charge of the reservoirs said.

title: Construction industry in severe crisis due to rising material prices: Construction Association
byline: The construction industry is facing a severe crisis due to the rapid increase in the prices of construction-related materials, Chairman of the Sri Lanka Construction Association (SLCA) Susantha Liyanarachchi said.

title: Provide relief packages for the micro, SMEs: Sajith
byline: While highlighting that the micro, small and medium enterprises have been severely affected by the fuel price hike, Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa today urged the government to come up with a relief package for them.

title: Iran stops pak-bound ship from crossing Hormuz over lack of permission
byline: A Pakistan-bound container ship has been stopped from crossing the Strait of Hormuz by Iranian forces amid the escalating war in the Middle East. The vessel, SELEN, sailing from the United Arab Emirates’ Sharjah anchorage toward Karachi, was forced to reverse course at the entrance to the crucial waterways due to the absence of transit authorisation, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

title: Ranil will have to take over country to manage present crisis: Rathnapriya
byline: Claiming that all the crisis situations faced by Sri Lanka in the past were managed by former President Ranil Wickremesinghe, former UNP MP Saman Rathnapriya said today the present crisis situation faced by the country will also have to be managed by Wickremesinghe.

title: Kim Jong Un uses Iran war to justify North Korea’s decision to keep its nuclear weapons
byline: North Korea’s Kim Jong Un has said the United States’ war with Iran proves his country made the right decision to keep its nuclear weapons.

title: Sharp temperature contrast across island as Nuwara Eliya drops to 7.8°C
byline: Sri Lanka experienced a marked contrast in minimum temperatures today (25), with Nuwara Eliya recording the country’s lowest at 7.8°C, the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Iran rejects US proposal, lays out five conditions for ending imposed war: Source
byline: Iran has responded negatively to an American proposal aimed at ending the ongoing imposed war, insisting that it will only occur on Tehran’s own terms and timeline, a senior political-security official told Press TV on Wednesday.

title: Iran military claims it fired missiles at USS Abraham Lincoln carrier
byline: Iran fired cruise missiles at the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier, the military said in a statement carried by state television, warning of further launches when the strike group’s ships come in range.

title: US 15-point plan reaches Tehran as Iran publicly scoffs at diplomacy
byline: Iran has received a US 15-point proposal via Pakistan aimed at opening a path toward a ceasefire, a senior Iranian source told Reuters on Wednesday, though the venue for any talks was still under discussion and Tehran publicly denied that negotiations with Washington had begun.

title: Suspect arrested for fuel QR code fraud in Nittambuwa
byline: A suspect has been arrested in Nittambuwa by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for allegedly overriding the fuel QR code of a woman’s vehicle and fraudulently obtaining fuel by generating a new QR code using the vehicle’s data.

title: Sanjeewa Dharmaratne appointed Acting IGP
byline: Senior Deputy Inspector General of Police Sanjeewa Dharmaratne has been appointed as the Acting Inspector General of Police.

title: CSE extends rally as strong buying momentum drives sharp gains
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange extended its upward momentum on 25th March 2026, building on the previous session’s strong rebound as investor optimism continued to strengthen. Elevated turnover and share volumes signaled a clear return of positive sentiment, with increased participation supporting the market’s sustained upward trajectory.

title: No reason for rice price hike; sufficient stocks available: Deputy Minister
byline: Agriculture and Livestock Deputy Minister Namal Karunaratne has assured that there is no reason to increase rice prices for the New Year season, as the country has sufficient stocks.

title: Iran’s military rejects Trump’s talk of negotiation, Israel and Iran launch airstrikes
byline: Israel and Iran exchanged airstrikes on Wednesday, as Iran’s military rejected President Donald Trump’s assertion the U.S. was in negotiations to end the war which has roiled energy and financial markets, saying the U.S. is negotiating with itself.

title: Man arrested over dangerous tricycle driving, animal cruelty
byline: A man was arrested by Chilaw Police following a road accident involving a tricycle driven in a dangerous manner on the Chilaw–Kurunegala road, police said.

title: Limited water capacity amid dry weather, NWSDB warns
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) says the limited capacity of water treatment plants has become a concern due to the increased demand for pipe-borne water during the current dry weather conditions.
